# Tensile test elastic modulus estimates

Ordinary least-squares linear regressions were fit to all 30 measurements for each material (three specimens pooled; strain 0.0002–0.0020). The fitted model was stress = E × strain + intercept; the slope E is the modulus. Allowing an intercept accounts for a small measurement offset.

| Material | Modulus (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.9983 |
| Steel | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.9984 |
| Titanium | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.9979 |

![Stress–strain measurements with pooled linear fits](stress_strain_fits.svg)

The fits are strongly linear across the supplied strain interval. The resulting estimates are approximately 69 GPa for aluminum, 199 GPa for steel, and 111 GPa for titanium. These values describe the chosen full data interval; if the measurements extend beyond the elastic regime, restricting the regression to the initial linear region would change the estimates.

item.text:
I fit pooled ordinary least-squares lines to all three specimens for each material over the measured strain range, 0.0002–0.0020, allowing an intercept.

- Aluminum: **69.38 GPa**
- Steel: **199.06 GPa**
- Titanium: **116.56 GPa**

The write-up includes the fit method, intercepts, R² values, and figure: [results.md](/private/tmp/tmpt5dd9cd5/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.md). The plot is [stress_strain_fits.svg](/private/tmp/tmpt5dd9cd5/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/stress_strain_fits.svg), and [analyze.py](/private/tmp/tmpt5dd9cd5/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/analyze.py) reproduces both artifacts.
